The test image shows a decayed soybean stem/root junction with:
- Gray-brown rotted stem tissue
- Small blue-gray glistening particles scattered on the stem surface (consistent with microsclerotia)
- Dead, desiccated stem with fibrous decay
- Characteristic "dusty" gray appearance on the stem

The reference Charcoal Rot images confirm: silvery-gray bleached stems with dark internal decay — the same pattern. The blue-gray sparkly particles in the test image are characteristic microsclerotia (*Macrophomina phaseolina*) that give charcoal rot its name.
